additional_info.subject: Reported issue
additional_info.body:
Why we could see with 3 active charging cars that we have for every outlet EVSE_NowPwr max 40kW? Shouldn't we provide 80kW for one of the three outlets? At Outlet 1, I noticed that the car requested a voltage of 423V, but we only delivered 386.5V. Why wasn't the full power of 40kW utilized?
Error Date & Time: 21-02-2025 11:12

additional_info.subject: RE: AW: 0409207 - ID0409207-DC/Si-D/AT- [Y2/S7 313782532001] Outlet 1 delivered less power CRM:02023000524
additional_info.body:
Dear Johannes Dissauer,
Thank you for your patients and response.
Regarding your first query, please find below the relevant log message:
2025-02-21, 10:12:04
2025-02-21T10:12:04.592223+00:00 swcpu [user: debug] [4021] [DCC] |2025-02-21T10:10:27|DC1: |EVSE_MaxPwr[kW]=80|EVSE_MaxCur[A]=126|EVSE_NowPwr[kW]=37.9|EVSE_NowCur[A]=99|EVSE_NowVol[V]=384.9|EV_TarCur[A]=99|EV_TarVol[V]=423|EV_SOC[%]=66|EVSE_DESpwr[kW]=160|Pilot=4
As indicated in the log, the power was initially allocated to 80 kW. However, the EV requested less power, leading the charger to automatically reduce the power to 40 kW. Please see the message below for reference:
Active CG Constellation type changed: CG(p+s1) -> CG(p), Max Sourcing Power(kW):
80 -> 40
For your second query regarding the target voltage, the voltage reflected in the logs represents the maximum battery voltage of the EV. As the state of charge (SOC) of the EV increases, the charger gradually increases the voltage to match the battery’s requirements.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Vikas Khiladkar
